Subject: Hosting path qualification and HIPAA/SOC2 audit action plan

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment: 

Summary of needs you outlined:
- Primary requirement: HIPAA-covered workload (PHI) for clinical triage product.
- Must sign a BAA and receive SOC 2 Type II evidence.
- Auditability: customer-visible audit logs and ability to pull event history for audits.
- Key technical asks: KMS/HSM support for key management, ability to isolate data at rest, and clear data retention/deletion policy.
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity or Private VPC, given isolation and compliance posture, but open to tradeoffs if Hosted API can meet controls.

What I’ll send you by end of day today: SOC2 Type II report (redacted), our standard BAA template, and a short checklist for private/on-prem onboarding.

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
1) We (Redwood) share SOC2 + BAA template and onboarding checklist — by COB today. [I will attach]
2) HealthBridge to complete and return the security questionnaire we discussed — target 2 weeks.
3) Technical deep dive with our infra/security engineer (Jonas) to cover KMS/HSM, VPC network topology, and audit log access — propose Tue 2026-11-17 or Wed 2026-11-18.
4) If Dedicated or Private is selected, coordinate procurement + PO + legal — estimated 3–6 weeks post-PO for Dedicated, 6–10+ weeks for Private on-prem.
5) Pilot/POC: 4–6 weeks from signature depending on scope (throughput, data residency).

Please confirm availability for the technical deep dive (Jonas is looped). If you prefer, we can also run a short internal security checklist call prior to the deep dive.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted), BAA_Template_Redwood_v3.docx, Private_Deployment_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf

Thanks —

Hi team / Emma —

Quick technical clarifications to answer Emma’s questions ahead of the deep dive: 

KMS/HSM: 
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed KMS via standard cloud KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key). We can also configure HSM-backed keys where the cloud provider/hardware supports it.
- Private VPC (Redwood-managed in your cloud account): we support VPC peering and KMS integration; policy depends on whether the keys remain in your tenant. For an on-prem Private deployment, keys are fully customer controlled.

Audit logs and access: 
- We expose structured audit logs for request/response metadata and infra events. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can receive a read-only export of audit logs to their secure storage (S3/GCS) on a configurable cadence (daily/weekly).
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): we provide operational logs but do not expose full tenant-level raw request logs by default; we offer sanitized traces and usage-level telemetry.

Data deletion: 
- Standard data deletion window for ephemeral request data: purge request handled within 72 hours; confirmed deletion from hot caches within 24 hours for Dedicated/Private.
- For backups/snapshots we provide documented retention and an eradication plan; Private on-prem gives you direct control and fastest verifiability.

Tradeoffs and timelines: 
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding (hours), lowest operational burden, lowest isolation guarantees.
- Dedicated: balance of isolation + speed — typically 3–6 weeks to provision and validate (depending on region and capacity), supports KMS and log exports.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): highest isolation and control; onboarding 6–12+ weeks depending on network/ops approvals and any on-prem hardware procurement.

Attachments I’m sharing internally: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (redacted), BAA_Template_Redwood_v3.docx, Private_Deployment_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf

I’ll cover architecture sketches and sample network diagrams in the deep dive.

—Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Emma —

Thanks — confirmed: technical deep dive booked for Tue 2026-11-17 at 10:30 PT (30–45m). Jonas will walk through KMS/HSM options, audit log exports, and our deletion/retention controls.

Attached is a short mutual action plan to make approvals predictable. Please review and flag any internal blockers. High-level plan: 
- Week 0 (this week): Redwood sends SOC2 + BAA + onboarding checklist (done).
- Week 1–2: HealthBridge completes security questionnaire and schedules any follow-up calls (you).
- Week 2–3: Technical deep dive + sample architecture review (Redwood + HealthBridge infra).
- Week 3–4: BAA signature + procurement (legal + finance).
- Week 4–8: Provision Dedicated capacity or Private VPC (depending on selection) and run POC (joint acceptance criteria).

POC scope options (pick one for estimate):
A) Low-latency inference test: 50 concurrent sessions, 2M tokens/day — Dedicated recommended.
B) Full production pilot with PHI: Private VPC or Dedicated with strict KMS + logging — recommended for go-live.

Next actions for HealthBridge (for the deep dive):
- Share completed security questionnaire (HealthBridge_SecQ-for-Redwood.xlsx).
- Confirm whether your legal team prefers redlines to the BAA template or an executed copy.

I’ll drop these items into HubSpot and send a DocuSign BAA link after the deep dive if that works.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_HealthBridge_Redwood_v1.pdf (attached), see prior SOC2/BAA files.

Best,
Neha
